trajectory_summary: The call opens cooperatively, moves through a fairly mechanical verify sequence, and ends in a hard DQ once the rep clarifies the home is a manufactured home on a foundation. The rep caught the disqualifier via a hold-and-check rather than in real time, and closed the call flatly with no bridge, no cross-sell mention despite a six-car garage and woodsheds on the property, and no acknowledgment of the customer's stated fixed-income status.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unspecified; observed outcome is a clean hard DQ (manufactured home) — not a missed appointment due to rep error, but a legitimate disqualification. The call should not be scored as a booking failure; the shape read reflects flat, procedural execution around a valid DQ rather than a collapsed sales attempt.

observed_outcome.quote: Hey. So it looks like we actually don't work with manufactured homes, so solar may not be the best option for you k.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep explicitly disqualifies the customer due to manufactured-home construction after checking with someone during the hold, ending the call with no appointment set.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the bill figure but moved immediately to the next verify item ('have you seen a solar design for your home yet?') without reflecting it back or using it to build interest; the flip should have gone right after '02:52' before moving to prior-design question.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: There was an ad on the Internet that Colorado gave you 30,000 to put on solar.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked what interested the customer in solar and got a clear reason (a Colorado incentive ad), then correctly identified it as the tax credit, but never returned to reinforce this motivation later in the call — especially relevant once the customer revealed he doesn't file taxes, which directly undercut the very incentive that drew him in, and the rep never addressed that tension.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: real-time DQ recognition on property type
primary_coaching_focus.quote: The garage is a six car garage, and the house is either manufactured home on a foundation.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep didn't act on the manufactured-home disclosure until after finishing the entire verify sequence (utility, bill, prior design), running the customer through several more minutes of questions on a lead that was very likely already disqualified — catching this immediately would have respected the customer's time either way.

key_moments.quote: The garage is a six car garage, and the house is either manufactured home on a foundation.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep did not recognize this as a likely hard-DQ trigger in the moment and continued through the rest of the verify sequence (utility, bill, prior design) before checking. Reactive read: rep missed the significance and defaulted to finishing the script. Strategic read considered: rep may have wanted the full picture before interrupting flow — but the ~90 second hold at 03:02 to check on exactly this detail confirms it was not caught until after the fact.

key_moments.quote: Let me check into one thing real quick, Tyler. I'm just gonna put you on hold. I'll be right back. Okay? Sure.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies the manufactured-home detail as needing verification against Ion's policy rather than guessing or promising something Ion can't deliver, and puts the customer on hold to confirm rather than bluffing through the call.

Customer volunteers a fixed-income/retirement signal directly in response to the tax-incentive framing. The rep's next line, 'You're retired? Okay,' acknowledges the fact but does not bridge to why solar could still matter for a fixed-income household, nor does it soften the pitch to that reality.

key_moments.quote: so solar may not be the best option for you k.
key_moments.stewart_read: The DQ delivery is functional but flat — 'may not be the best option' with a trailing 'k' reads as rushed rather than a considered close. The schema has no defined DQ-close protocol, which is itself a gap: there is no scripted warmth/next-step language for hard disqualifications like this one.
